summary: Adolf Ellegard Jensen worked in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied under Leo Frobenius (~1923–1938) and held posts at the Frobenius Institute (1923–1939, 1946–1965), Museum der Weltkulturen (1936–1965), and Goethe University Frankfurt (1946–1965).

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Berlin (PhD 1826–1829), Greifswald, Bonn, and Paris under Bopp, Schlegel, Lassen, Kosegarten, and others. He worked at the East India Company (~1830–1833) and University of Breslau (1833–1872).

Adolf Holtzmann specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Munich under Othmar Frank and Johann Andreas Schmeller, Berlin, and under Eugène Burnouf (~1837–1838). From 1852 to 1870, he served as a professor at Heidelberg University.

Adolf Kaegi was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Zurich, Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth, and Leipzig, as well as under Karl Friedrich Geldner. He held multiple academic posts at the University of Zurich from 1875 to 1914.

Adolf Kirchhoff worked in linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1842–1846) under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He held posts at Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium (1846), Prussian Academy of Sciences (1860), and Berlin (~1865–1908).
Adolf Noreen was a linguist who studied at Uppsala University (~1871–1877) and under August Leskien (~1879). He held a post at Uppsala University from ~1877 to 1919.

Adolph Kießling was a scholar in linguistics and other fields. He studied under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker (~1856–1858) and held posts at the University of Basel (~1869–1877), University of Greifswald (~1877–1889), and University of Göttingen.

Adolphe Regnier worked in Indology, linguistics, and other fields, studying under Eugène Burnouf. He held positions at the Collège de France (1838), École Normale Supérieure (1841–1843), Académie des Inscriptions et Belles-Lettres (1855), and Palace of Fontainebleau (1873).

Adriaan Scharpé was an Indologist who earned his doctoral degree at Utrecht University (~1934–1937) under Jan Gonda. He held posts as an assistant professor at the University of Amsterdam (1947–1978) and professor at Ghent University (~1948–1978).
Adrian Kuzminski is a scholar in philosophy and Indology. He taught at the University of Hawaiʻi and served as a resident scholar in philosophy at Hartwick College in 1997.

Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and sinology. He studied at the University of Auckland and the University of Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger (PhD ~2006–2011), later holding posts at the European School of Culture and Theology and Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation.

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and University of Bonn (1995), and holds an affiliation at the University of Warsaw (attested 2008 and 2026).

Agehananda Bharati was a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1945–1948), taught across India and Japan in the 1950s, and was Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian Studies at Syracuse University (1961–1991).

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny specializes in Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts, Warsaw, and Nicolaus Copernicus University (PhD ~2003–2007), holding posts at Cornell University (attested 2009) and the University of Warsaw (2015).

Agvan Dorjiev was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang (1880–1888), earning the Geshe-Lharampa degree. He founded Datsan Gunzechoinei and taught the 13th Dalai Lama and Geshe Wangyal.

Agvan Dorzhiev was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a Geshey Lharampa degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang in 1873, founded Atsagat Datsan in 1913, and taught Geshe Wangyal and the 13th Dalai Lama.

Ahmad Hasan Dani was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Banaras Hindu University, London, and under Altekar, Wheeler, and Codrington. He held posts at Dhaka, University of Peshawar (1962–1971), and Quaid-i-Azam University (1971, 1997).

Aiko Okoshi was a scholar in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University (~1970–1975) and served as a full-time lecturer at Kindai University beginning in 1990.

Ajahn Amaro is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. He studied at Bedford College, trained under Ajahn Chah and Ajahn Sumedho, co-founded and served as co-abbot of Abhayagiri Buddhist Monastery (~1996–2010), and became abbot of Amaravati in ~2010.

Ajahn Brahm specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at Emmanuel College, Cambridge (~1969–1972) and trained under Nai Boonman and Ajahn Chah (1974), later becoming the abbot of Bodhinyana Monastery in ~1995.
